comments.body: Interesting! Note, even though it happens to be reported by TSan, it's a plain null-deref crash (`SEGV on unknown address 0x000000000000`) not (a priori) a threading-related issue --- in other words, for all we know at this point, this looks like a general crash that might as well have occured in any non-TSan config.

Stack frame 2 is: https://github.com/iree-org/iree/blob/90bed7e145d7edf8496ba79745989a76ffe0443a/runtime/src/iree/task/executor.c#L224

But stack frame 1 says that `iree_atomic_ref_count_dec` was given a null pointer - meaning that `&executor->ref_count` is NULL. A look at `executor_impl.h` shows that `ref_count` is at offset 0 in `executor` so that's equivalent to saying that `executor` is NULL.

But the code at stack frame 2 is checking that `executor` is not NULL before proceeding:
```
if (executor && iree_atomic_ref_count_dec(&executor->ref_count) == 1) {
```

So how can this null deref happen? One can guess that some other thread wrote NULL to `executor` after the first part of the above `if` and before the second part. In normal (non-TSan), optimized code, that would never happen, because the pointer value `executor` would be read once from memory into a register used by both parts of that `if` condition, so any data race would be papered over. I guess that the way that TSan helps uncover the issue here is that it prevents optimizing away memory accesses, allowing for the two parts of that `if` to get inconsistent values for `executor`.

If that theory is correct, TSan should have reported a data race on `executor` instead of continuing into the null deref.  (I checked the full log, it really didn't catch the data race per se). Don't know why it didn't, but TSan is notoriously a "best effort" sanitizer. Good, anyway, that it allowed the data race to cause inconsistent accesses, allowing us to catch the bug nonetheless.

issue.body:
This loop is already handling EAGAIN. It looks like it should handle EINTR the same way.

I'm trying to guess what might cause the intermittent crash #10337. One thing that would explain it is if the iree_task_scope_wait_idle done at the end of SubmitTasksAndWaitIdle wasn't doing its job. It calls iree_notification_await, which assumes that
iree_notification_commit_wait never returns false unless the deadline is exceeded. But iree_notification_commit_wait does return false if the futex syscall returns an expected error code, so we need to handle the exhaustive list of return codes that might come out of this syscall. The manual page lists only very few possible return codes for the particular FUTEX_WAIT op we're doing here (there are plenty of error cases, but few apply to FUTEX_WAIT). EINTR is the only one that I could see us missing here.
